Forecast Discussion

High pressure over Virginia keeps us dry today. High clouds spread north from low pressure forming near Florida.

That low moves north along the Carolina coast Saturday and Saturday night as our high shifts to New England. An easterly flow brings more clouds and a cooler Saturday.

We are on the western fringe of its rain late Saturday night and Sunday morning. Light rain is mostly near the Blue Ridge. The low pulls away Sunday afternoon.

A front crosses from the west Monday. A few showers come with it, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians.

Tuesday is dry and colder as high pressure builds to our north.

Low pressure then develops to our south. Meanwhile, cold air wedges down the east side of the Appalachians, anchored by high pressure centered in New England. Rain is possible by late Tuesday night, increasing Wednesday into Wednesday night. It may become cold enough late Wednesday for the highest elevations to mix with snow at times.

Cold air is reinforced from the west on Thanksgiving Day. Rain tapers to showers, and snow showers may mix in at higher elevations.
